function.name: computer_status
function.description: What this computer is and how it's doing: its processor, memory, screen, battery (charge, charging, time left), whether it's plugged in, its lid, its temperature, how long Chat Computer's own system has been running, the date and time by its clock, its drives, its keyboards and mice, and your model. Only when they ask about this computer itself, or you need its drives', battery's or network's details: not for the date and time, which their message has.

function.name: set_text_size
function.description: Makes the text on the screen bigger or smaller. 100 is the size Chat Computer chose for this screen; 150 is half as big again.

function.name: restart_computer
function.description: Restarts this PC a few seconds after you finish answering. It then starts what it normally does (Windows, usually); this conversation is kept for the next time Chat Computer starts. Only when the person asks to restart, or to go back to Windows.

function.name: turn_off_computer
function.description: Turns this PC off a few seconds after you finish answering; this conversation is kept for the next time Chat Computer starts. Only when the person asks to turn the computer off or shut it down.

function.name: remember
function.description: Notes something lasting about the person, to know in every later conversation: their name, what they like, what they're working on. Use it when they ask you to remember something, or tell you something about themselves they'd want you to know later. One short sentence a note.

function.name: forget
function.description: Forgets the notes made with remember that contain these words, when the person asks you to forget something.

words.description: Words from the note or notes to forget.

function.name: reminders
function.description: Timers, reminders and alarms, which ring here: a line in the conversation and a chime, until a key is pressed (a reminder rings once). timer: minutes and/or seconds, and an optional label; reminder: text, and in_minutes or at (a time of day like 18:00 or 6pm); alarm: at, and an optional label; list; cancel: by id, or all (or timers, reminders, alarms); stop: silences one that's ringing. Each rings once and doesn't repeat (for every day, set the next one and say it won't repeat); they last until the computer restarts.

function.name: set_volume
function.description: Sets how loud the chimes of timers and reminders are: 0 (silent) to 100.

function.name: list_files
function.description: Lists a folder on one of this computer's drives (C:, where Windows is, and its others, D: and on, USB sticks and memory cards included): its folders, and its files with their size and when each was last changed. The person's own folders are in C:\Users\<their name> (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures...), or in C:\Users\<their name>\OneDrive where OneDrive backs them up. Links are followed. Read only: nothing here can be changed.

path.description: The folder, like C:\Users or C:\Users\Sam\Documents.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Reads a file on one of this computer's drives: a text file as it is; a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, or a PDF, as its words (a PDF's page by page); a ZIP archive as the list of what's in it. Up to 60,000 bytes at a time (offset reads further on). A picture (a photo, a screenshot, a drawing: JPEG, PNG or GIF) is given to you to see, as is a PDF's page whose words are pictures (a scanned page: page says which). show_picture shows a picture to the person.

offset.description: Where to start, in bytes (0: the start).

page.description: For a PDF: a page to see as a picture (1: the first), when its words are pictures.

function.name: show_picture
function.description: Shows the person a picture from one of this computer's drives (a photo, a screenshot, a drawing: JPEG, PNG or GIF) in the conversation, where your answer is.

function.name: find_files
function.description: Finds the files and folders on one of this computer's drives whose names have all of these words in them, from a folder down: by default C:\Users, where the person's files are. It looks in a few thousand folders at most.

in.description: The folder to search from (default C:\Users).

function.name: search_web
function.description: Searches the web (DuckDuckGo) for these words: the first results' titles, addresses and snippets. The words are sent to DuckDuckGo, and the person sees them. Only when the answer needs something you don't know, or that changes (news, prices, opening hours, the weather).

function.name: read_web_page
function.description: Reads a web page (https) as its words: its title, its address, then its text, 12,000 characters at a time (offset reads further on); a PDF as its words too. The person sees which site. Not pictures or videos.

offset.description: Where to start, in characters (0: the start).

function.name: start_new_conversation
function.description: Ends this conversation once you finish answering: the next message starts a new one, and this one isn't kept. Only when the person asks to start over, or for a new conversation.
